name: Shemaiah
overview: Shemaiah is a male biblical figure uniquely identified as the father of Uriah and associated with Kiriath-jearim, as recorded in Jeremiah 26:20. There is no tribal affiliation or additional notes provided about him. His mention is brief but specific, anchoring him in a particular family and location.
namesAndTitles: The name Shemaiah means 'YHWH hears,' reflecting a theophoric element common in Hebrew names that acknowledges God's attentive nature. This single proper name is the only one recorded for him and is not indicated to have been given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Shemaiah primarily as the father of Uriah, based on Jeremiah 26:20. Beyond this paternal relationship, no other family connections are documented for him in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Shemaiah's significance lies in his role as the progenitor of Uriah from Kiriath-jearim, situating him within the prophetic narrative of Jeremiah. His mention helps identify Uriah's lineage and geographical background, contributing to the historical and theological context of the events described in Jeremiah. Though his personal story is not expanded upon, his connection to Uriah anchors a key figure in the unfolding biblical account.
